52-018.r: Uttar Pradesh ranks first in production of Wheat and Sugarcane (Agricultural Statistics at a Glance 2024-25).

52-019.r: Sharbati Sonora → induced-mutation (gamma-ray) wheat from Sonora-64 at IARI. Mexican dwarf wheats brought in: Lerma Rojo 64-A, Sonora-63, Sonora 64, Mayo 64, S227.
52-019.c: Sonora-64 is an imported Mexican dwarf wheat. IARI irradiated it (gamma rays) to get the amber-grained mutant Sharbati Sonora, option (c), the standard answer for induced mutation.

52-020.r: Dwarfing genes: Norin-10 → wheat; Dee-gee-woo-gen → rice; Opaque-2 → maize.

52-021.r: Macaroni wheat → most suitable under rainfed conditions.

52-022.r: Raj 3077 → late-sown wheat variety (36-40 quintals per hectare). Other wheats: Sonalika, Arjun, Kundan.

52-023.r: Pusa Sindhu Ganga (HD 2967) → wheat variety, identified at the 48th All India Wheat and Barley Research Workers Meet, IARI.

52-024.r: UP-308 → Mexican dwarf wheat variety (used mainly in Darbhanga district, Bihar).

52-025.r: Wheat output 2006-07 to 2009-10 → steady upward trend: 75.81 → 78.57 → 80.68 → 80.80 million tonnes.

52-026.r: Indira Sona → hybrid rice (not wheat) of Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur; its wheat varieties: Ratan, Kanishka, Ambar, Vidya.

52-027.r: Wheat disease → Rust (Yellow, Brown and Black rust).

52-028.r: Kalyana Sona → high-yielding variety of wheat.

52-029.r: Wheat varieties: Arjun, Sonalika; rice varieties: Jaya, Padma.

52-030.r: Arhar (pigeon pea) for double cropping with wheat → U.P.A.S-120; other Arhar varieties: Bahar, ICPL-151, ICPL-87.

52-031.r: Book's true set (1, 2, 3): UP top wheat producer; rice-wheat is UP's largest cropping pattern. False: flowering as most critical wheat irrigation stage → it is CRI stage.

52-032.r: Triticale → cross (hybrid) between Wheat and Rye (Rai).

52-033.r: Punjab, Haryana, UP are major wheat states (A true); wheat needs well-drained fertile soil, cool winter, about 75 cm rain (R true); book: R not the explanation.

52-034.r: Karnal bunt → fungal disease of wheat caused by Tilletia indica; first identified 1931.

52-035.r: Macaroni wheat → botanical name Triticum durum.

52-036.r: Herbicide → Butachlor; Chlorpyrifos and Quinolphos → pesticides; Carbendazim → fungicide.

53-001.r: Rice → originated in South-East Asia; needs temperature above 25°C and rainfall above 100 cm.

53-002.r: Wrong pair: Bihar — 15.7% of rice production. True: West Bengal grows rice three times a year; UP largest rice area; 100 cm isohyet marks rice's western limit.

53-003.r: System of Rice Intensification (alternate wetting and drying; from Madagascar, 1980s) → less seed, less methane, less electricity → all three.

53-004.r: Kharif crops: cotton, groundnut, rice (sown June-July, harvested September-October); wheat is Rabi.

53-005.r: Not a Rabi pulse → Green gram (moong; Kharif, sown late June-early July). Rabi pulses: gram (chickpea), lentil, pea, lathyrus, French bean.

53-006.r: Ideal rice climate → rainfall above 100 cm, temperature above 25°C, high humidity; irrigation where rain is less.

53-007.r: Soyabean → Kharif; Lentil, Linseed, Mustard, Gram → not Kharif. Kharif also: rice, maize, cotton, groundnut, jute. Zaid: muskmelon, watermelon, cucumber.

53-010.r: Chief food crop of India → Rice; Wheat is second.

53-011.r: Largest cropped area among food crops → Rice (51.27 million ha, 2024-25); Wheat 32.80 million ha.

53-013.r: Largest area under rice cultivation → Uttar Pradesh (7.35 million ha, 2024-25).

53-014.r: Rice yield 2013-14 → 2416 kg/ha, so 'None of these'; in 2024-25 → 2929 kg/ha.

53-015.r: Rice Bowl of India (among options) → Krishna-Godavari delta, Andhra Pradesh.
53-015.c: The book calls Rayalseema the rice area on the Krishna-Godavari delta; the delta is in coastal Andhra, while Rayalaseema is the dry interior region.

53-017.r: Not a rice variety → Jawala. Rice varieties: Jaya, Padma, Hansa, Krishna, Jamuna, Kaveri, Annapurna, Ratna.

53-019.r: Aman rice → sown June-July, harvested November-December (winter crop); Aus → May-June to September-October (autumn); Boro → November-December to March-April (summer).

53-020.r: Pusa Sugandha-5 → aromatic variety of rice.

53-021.r: Barani deep → paddy (rice) variety; others: Narendra Sankar, Narendra Shuska Samrat, Lalmati.

53-022.r: Hybrid Basmati rice → Pusa RH-10; other hybrids: PHB-71, Ganga, Suruchi, KRH-2, Sahyadri-4.

53-023.r: Seed rate for transplanting Basmati rice → 15-20 kg per hectare.

53-024.r: Punjab → major rice exporter (A true) but not the top producer (R false). Variant then: West Bengal largest; 2024-25: Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, West Bengal.

53-026.r: Biofertilizer for rice → Blue-green algae (also Azospirillum, Azolla, Phosphobacteria).

53-027.r: East coast grows more rice (suitable climate, soil) → A true; West coast gets more rainfall (narrow, high mountains) → R false.

53-028.r: Crop whose cultivated area stayed more or less stagnant in the decade before 2010 → Rice (book's answer).
53-028.c: The book's own table shows rice area rising (42.9 → 45.8 → 51.27 million ha) and sugarcane flat (4.9 → 4.9); the answer fits the earlier decade, not this data.

53-029.r: More than half of India's rice → West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh.

53-030.r: Rice production ascending (when asked): Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal (3, 2, 1, 4). 2024-25 (Mt): TN 7.09, AP 8.16, Punjab 14.36, WB 16.02.

53-031.r: Surplus rice producer → Andhra Pradesh (highest market surplus ratio, 2008-09); in 2024-25 Punjab tops.

53-032.r: Rice → cultivated where annual rainfall is over 100 cm (higher water need than any other crop).

53-033.r: Largest area under hybrid rice cultivation → Uttar Pradesh.

53-034.r: Four major rice producers (when asked): West Bengal, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh. 2024-25 top three: Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, West Bengal.

53-035.r: Rice production descending (when asked): West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh. 2024-25 (Mt): UP 20.76, Telangana 17.45, WB 16.02, Punjab 14.36.

53-036.r: Highest rice yield per hectare → Punjab (4428 kg/hectare, 2024-25).
